songs.title: The Spare Key on the Fridge
songs.intendedFeel: slow two-step pulse; relaxed syncopation; sustained open vowels

lines: You left a spare key where the magnets make a line,
Between the grocery list and a faded paper sign.
We never made a ceremony out of coming through the door,
We learned the sound of footsteps on the old upstairs floor.
One night the hallway filled with boxes stacked in rows,
You held the smallest lamp and asked which way the sofa goes.
I didn't know the answer, and you laughed without a sound,
Then set the lamp beside the chair and knelt to clear the ground.
The windows don't fit perfectly, the cupboard doesn't close,
But you know which loose floorboard creaks before the kettle goes.
Leave the light where we can find it,
Leave a little room beside it.
If the day gets loud and long,
There's a quiet place where we belong.
In April we were arguing about a coat left in the rain,
You went outside to get it while I counted every stain.
You came back with a photograph you'd found below the stair,
Two strangers in this kitchen from a year we weren't here.
They'd written on the border, "Keep the table if you can,"
So we sanded down the scratches with a borrowed little fan.
You signed beneath the picture in your unambitious hand,
And called the narrow kitchen something close to what we'd planned.
Keep the light where we can find it,
Set a bigger table by it.
When the day gets loud and long,
There's more than room for us to belong.
The spare key on the fridge door hardly shines against the white,
But I turn it in the lock and know that someone left a light.
Not a promise that the weather or the years will all be kind—
Just a place to put our burdens and a door we chose to find.

songs.title: The Platform Is a Drum
songs.intendedFeel: alternating call-response, percussion-first pocket, group refrain

lines: LEAD: A bucket and a bench—who brought the beat?
GROUP: The baker from the corner with the flour on his feet.
LEAD: Who found the backbeat hiding under station four?
GROUP: The guard who shuts the shutters when he closes up the door.
DANCER: I mark the stones in patterns while the evening buses stall.
My left foot keeps the high notes; my right can catch the fall.
You tell me I should stand still when the traffic lights turn red—
But a pause is just a doorway for the next beat in my head.
DRUMMER: My brother taught me rhythm with a pencil and a tin.
I learned to hear the spaces where the quieter drums begin.
Don't need a wall of thunder if the pocket has a place;
I let the final snare hit twice, then leave the room some space.
GROUP: Tap the rail, answer back.
GROUP: Hear the wheel upon the track.
LEAD: One small sound can start the floor.
GROUP: Leave some room for one beat more.
VIOLINIST: The strings can float above it with a note that bends and leans.
I start outside the downbeat, cut between the marching feet.
The drummer drops to silence; now my bow can barely sing—
He catches my last whisper with a soft tap on the rim.
GUARD: The final bus is pulling up. The driver shakes his head.
He says the neighbors need their sleep; the hour's past the end.
LEAD: We nod and pack the instruments, then move toward the square;
The rhythm takes the staircase, but the platform keeps the air.
GROUP: Tap the rail, then let it rest.
LEAD: The quiet part is not a test.
ALL: Tomorrow has another track.
ALL: And every echo carries back.

songs.title: The Little Window Upstairs
songs.intendedFeel: gentle three-pulse or 6/8 sway; lyric doesn't assert performed meter

lines: A little window upstairs,
A ribbon caught in the breeze,
The city folds away its noise
Among the sleeping trees.
Your blanket holds the moonlight
In squares upon the wall,
And somewhere in the courtyard
The latest raindrops fall.
Rest, little wanderer, rest,
The street can find its way.
The trains will take their journeys;
You can save yours for the day.
The neighbor turns a page,
A kettle settles down,
The washing lines are holding
The softest shirts in town.
No one needs an answer,
No race must yet be run;
A dream can take the long way
And still arrive with sun.
Sleep, little wanderer, sleep,
The windows know the rain.
The trains can keep their journeys;
You'll have your own again.
One lamp beneath the curtain,
One hand beside your hand,
A quiet little harbor
No map has ever planned.

songs.title: Room for the Fifth Beat
songs.intendedFeel: intended five-count phrasing on selected hook lines, variable resets; not audio-confirmed

lines: Every room in the warehouse is marked with chalk,
Every footstep echoes when the night crew walks.
One light flickers twice, then it waits for a third,
And the concrete keeps the shape of an unfinished word.
I count the steps from loading bay to painted door,
There used to be four; now the workers count one more.
The clock still tells us when to close the steel outside,
But nothing here explains why the echo will not hide.
One, two—hold it—three, four, five.
Leave the quiet part alive.
One, two—turn it—three, four, five.
That's the sound of getting by.
The oldest night watch walks the corridor alone,
Picks up an empty cup beside the telephone.
He taps the steel handrail where the ceiling lights go dark,
And hears a second answer from beyond the loading park.
He finds a loose board banging on the outer gate,
And tightens two old screws before it gets too late.
When the machinery returns to its ordinary chime,
The missing little silence feels as strange as missing time.
Count less.
Listen more.
Hear the hinges
On the door.
Breathe once.
Wait and see—
No floor can hold a rhythm
If it leaves no room for me.
One, two—let go—three, four, five.
Leave the quiet part alive.
One, two—slow down—three, four, five.
Now the whole room feels alive.
